title: DeepSeek and Huawei Take Aim at Nvidia’s Formidable Moat
source_used: The Business Times (Bloomberg Opinion column by Catherine Thorbecke, excerpt) and The Next Web (relaying Reuters, SCMP, NYT, Bloomberg on the underlying release)
key_facts: Bloomberg Opinion columnist Catherine Thorbecke argues DeepSeek and Huawei are chipping away at one of Nvidia's key advantages in China, its software.
DeepSeek has redeveloped its TileLang tools for Huawei's Ascend platform and made them freely available.
The tie-up could make it easier for Chinese AI firms still using American hardware to switch to home-grown alternatives.
Nvidia's software ecosystem has long given developers a reason to stay with its chips even as Huawei ramps up domestic shipments.
Underlying event: DeepSeek announced the Ascend tools on Wednesday 30 Sep 2026 via WeChat; Reuters reported six modules and a 128-chip Ascend 950 'supernode' built with Huawei (The Next Web).
quote_evidence: DeepSeek has redeveloped its TileLang tools for Huawei's Ascend platform – and is making them freely available for others to use.
The Hangzhou-based AI model maker and the Shenzhen telecommunications giant are teaming up on software, an underappreciated source of Nvidia's continued global dominance.
why_it_matters_hint: Nvidia's lead rests partly on software, and a free alternative for Huawei chips targets that lead.
notes: Bloomberg page blocked (403); excerpt only of the column read via Business Times syndication; underlying event details from The Next Web. This is an opinion column, not news reporting.
